Tech Report: The 8 Best Air Purifiers for Your Home

📅 29 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Industry observers note that clean indoor air has become more notable than ever.
  • Sources indicate that we got our hands on air purifiers from brands like Coway, Levoit, and GermGuardian and put them to the test.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Industry observers note that clean indoor air has become more notable than ever. While allergens like dust, dander, mold, and bacteria are all teaming up to infiltrate the air you breathe, the widespread wildfire smoke affecting much of the U.S. right now is also proving just how swiftly outdoor pollution can make its way inside. According to the EPA, Americans spend about 90 percent of their time indoors, where pollutant concentrations can sometimes be even higher than they are outside. An air purifier protects your airways from airborne irritants while providing clean, fresh air indoors (which is why we think everyone should invest in an air purifier).

Sources indicate that we got our hands on air purifiers from brands like Coway, Levoit, and GermGuardian and put them to the test. Filtration was our main concern, so we could determine the air purifiers’ efficiency. Then we moved along to other factors such as noise while running, how well they work in a given room, and convenience features. After our in-home testing, these are the air purifiers that came out on top.

Sources indicate that we tried out several air purifiers with a range of filtration systems, noise levels, and features. We tested these models in multiple different apartments, placing them in various rooms of the home to measure their efficiency. We considered the different uses of an air purifier, like if you’re an allergy sufferer or have a home filled with furry friends, and tested special features like light-up displays and automatic shutoff to determine their ease of use and effectiveness. We considered the amount of time it took to set up the different purifiers and install their filter systems.

In a recent development, for units that we haven’t tested, we combed through dozens of potential products and their specifications, reviews, and user complaints to identify what we thought were the best air purifiers. We settled on the following list, which includes options that are budget-friendly, sleekly designed, and high-performing.

The Airmega Mighty2 is the latest version of our previous Best Overall pick, the Coway AP-1512HH. The newest model combines power, quality filters, and robust controls to help you breathe easier.

The Mighty2 uses a three-stage filtration system to capture 99.7 percent of airborne particles, and cleans spaces up to 1,800 square feet in 60 minutes. It has three standard fan speeds, but there’s a turbo mode that will kick on if there’s a big uptick of matter in the air.

The original version just used an indicator light system that let you know basic air quality levels, but this updated model has a built-in air quality index sensor that measures and displays particulate matter counts in real time.

Industry observers note that our tester tried the air purifier in his Newly introduced York apartment, putting it up against pet odors, litterbox dust, and other household allergens. “Results after about a day were already noticeable. The air in the room seemed clearer and there was less dust on the ground in the area immediately around the litterbox. Not enough that I’m going to have to sweep up any less, mind you, but there was a material difference that I wasn’t getting from using a smaller purifier.”.

Full Coway Airmega Mighty2 Air Purifier Review.

This air purifier from Clorox uses a three-stage filtration system to trap allergens, pollutants, and VOCs, and it successfully cleared strong scents and odors from the apartment we tested in.

It was quiet enough that you hardly hear it activate, especially if it kicks on automatically while you’re cooking to clear the kitchen of smoke. But on higher settings, you do tend to notice its noise a bit more. The 360-degree, cylindrical shape of the filter offers purification from all directions, and the unit covers 1,000 square feet so you don't have to be as strategic about placement.

We also liked that it has a color-coded indicator light on the front that tells you how hazardous the air is in the room where it's located (though it will add insult to injury when it turns purple while you’re trying your best to sear a steak.).

Full Clorox Air Purifier Review.

It has been revealed that if you’re a pet owner, specifically with cats, then you know that the litter box smell lingers long after your little fur ball has left the lavatory. The Vital 200S-P from Levoit is a great way to combat the odors that candles and air fresheners just can’t cover up. I set the air purifier up in my living room and noticed a clear improvement in scent after running for the day.

This unit has a traditional air inlet, along with a unique U-shaped inlet that is ideal for trapping pet hair without clogging up the filters. If you pair your air purifier with the app and select Pet Mode, it automatically alternates between fan speeds, too. The pre-filter is easy to remove and wash, so you don't have to purchase replacements as often.

Since we tested the Vital 200S-P in a smaller apartment, it was a bit obtrusive. But the air purifier covers up to 1,875 square feet, so if you live in a townhouse or single-family home, this unit will accommodate.

Full Levoit Vital 200S-P Air Purifier Review.

Industry observers note that the Airmega 100 is the first cylindrical unit in the Coway line, which is a nice switch-up from the rectangular model that we tested in the past. It tucked nicely into the corner of the living room, and you can change the light between blue, orange, and off, which is ideal if you’re using the purifier in a bedroom.

I tried the fan on various settings, and the lowest mode could barely be heard over the TV playing at an average volume, which aligns with its claimed 20-decibel noise level. You can manually adjust everything on the control panel, or let the purifier do its thing and adapt accordingly as it monitors the air quality of the room.

Recent findings suggest that setup of the unit was simple; you essentially just need to click the filter into place. This model uses a 3-in-1 filtration system, with a HEPA filter sandwiched between a vacuumable pre-filter and deodorizing filter. The deodorizer layer is especially useful if you have pets, love to cook, or live in an apartment or complex with odors.

Full Coway Airmega 100 Air Purifier Review.

For smaller rooms or office spaces, the smart Blueair 511i Max offers much of the same performance and features as larger, more capable models. It only purifies areas of up to 465 square feet, but does so within just 30 minutes on the highest setting. The three-layer filtration system captures up to 99.7 percent of airborne particles, too.

In a recent development, we appreciate that the air quality level is clearly displayed on the front in a five-color scale, and that the display has auto-brightness controls if you're running it overnight while you're sleeping. Advanced features are available through the app, including scheduling and air quality reports.

This unit has a four-stage filtration system, along with Blueair's proprietary HEPASilent filter that uses a combination of electrostatic charge and mechanical filtration to capture 99.97 percent of airborne pollutants and contaminants. This type of filtration technology is less dense than other filter options, so it's designed to run quieter and use less energy.

The value offered by such a small air purifier is unmatched, considering it targets both allergens and odors—all with relatively quiet operation.

If you have a large space or even an entire apartment that needs air purification, the Coway Airmega 400 is the smart model you need. It's designed to cover up to 1,560 square feet in 30 minutes, and has a variety of smart features and sleep settings, all packed into a compact yet capable unit. While this is the most expensive option we recommend, it's relatively affordable considering its capacity, and you shouldn’t have to supplement with an additional air purifier.

Recent findings suggest that it’s surprisingly quiet given its size, reaching only 22 decibels on its lowest setting. We like that it uses multi-stage purification methods, combining a pre-filter, an activated carbon filter, and a True HEPA filter to capture the tiniest of particles. The pre-filter is washable, but the air filter indicator light will let you know when it actually needs to be replaced.

The Airmega 400 has a three-setting smart mode that adapts to its environment, with a fan speed that automatically adjusts based on air quality or lighting conditions. We also appreciate the option to use eco mode, which turns the fan on and off when the room has remained purified for 30 minutes, and there’s also a timer and pollution sensor.

The GermGuardian isn’t a flashy design with robust features, but it aids in keeping the air in my apartment free of pet odors, dust, and smoke.

Industry observers note that I have a self-cleaning litter box, which significantly cuts down on smells and dust associated with cat waste, but it doesn’t solve every problem. I let the purifier run during one of the Litter Robot’s cleaning cycles, and thanks to the GermGuardian’s built-in air quality index (AQI) sensor and display screen, I was able to see the particulate matter count in the air reach triple digits in seconds. The automatic fan speed varied as needed, and it wasn’t long before air quality was back to a healthy level.

I put the GermGuardian up against incense smoke, too, and it went to work promptly. The fan had to run at high speed for longer, but by the end, my living room was clear of any lingering haze and odor.

In addition to a HEPA filter and activated carbon, this model also has a UVC light, which is claimed to disinfect bacteria, viruses, and mold. While I did give this feature a try, I didn’t keep it on for long because it’s hard to prove whether these lights are actually useful in an air purifier.

Read Full GermGuardian AC4880B Air Purifier Review.

The Sans HEPA 13 air purifier offers quiet operation, whole-home purification, and smart features. This unit runs at only 25 decibels on the lowest fan setting, and I could hardly tell that it was on, even when standing next to the unit.

According to recent reports, the air purifier is best used for whole-home use, as it purifies spaces up to 1,854 square feet. The internal sensors monitor and show you the air quality index in real time, and the reading is visible on the touch display. I’m able to view PM2.5, which is particles that are 2.5 microns or smaller, such as dust, smoke, pollen, and pet dander, as well as PM10, which are slightly larger particles up to 10 microns, like coarser dust and mold spores.

Sources indicate that this unit pairs a medical-grade HEPA 13 filter with a pre-filter, activated carbon filter, and UV-C light to capture 99.9 percent of particles. This might be overkill for general household use, but I’ve appreciated the multi-stage approach. The only downside I’ve come across is that overall cost will likely be higher, considering the Sans recommends replacing the filter every three months.

There is no shortage of air purifiers on the market, and many of them use a lot of the same tech to achieve better air quality. We’re often testing many different models to find the top recommendations. Ahead are some that haven’t made it to this roundup, but are still worth considering.

It has been revealed that rabbit Air A3 Air Purifier: This air purifier uses a six-stage filtration system to rid your home of smoke, dander, odors, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and germs. The lowest fan setting clocks in around 20 decibels, which is extremely quiet, so you can run this model daily without being disturbed. The build is relatively bulky so it’s not the easiest to tuck into a corner and out of the way, and the $760 price tag is pretty steep.

Sources indicate that germGuardian AirSafe+ XL: This model is shaped like our best portable pick above, and comes with a lot of the same features as the other GermGuardian we recommend, and it has a companion app for tracking air quality metrics. That said, the app doesn’t specify what type or size particulate matter the sensor is measuring, so it’s hard to tell what common allergens are actually floating around your home.

Air purifiers vary in filtration range, so it's vital to first consider your room size before buying. To find a model that accommodates your space, the EPA recommends that you first multiply the length and width of the area where you intend to operate the air purifier to calculate the square footage.

Most air purifiers have a maximum coverage area listed, so just compare to your calculations to find an air purifier that is the best fit for your home.

In a recent development, if you have an open floor plan or high ceilings, opt for an air purifier with more coverage. You should also place the air purifier in the room you use most regularly, and make sure it’s in an area where the airflow isn’t obstructed.

It has been revealed that the filter system of your air purifier might differ depending on the model and concern you're trying to target such as allergy relief, odor elimination, or germ protection. You’ll often see three-stage filtration (or four-, five-, or six-stage), which includes all three of the filter types detailed below.

Pre-filters are typically the first line of defense in an air purifier and trap larger particles like dust, hair, and fur, which helps extend the lifespan of the main filter and improves the overall efficiency of the unit.

All of our selections on this list involve a multi-step filtration system to target a majority of common pollutants and allergens in your household.

Industry observers note that purvi Parikh, MD, an allergist and immunologist with NYU Langone Health, recommends selecting an air purifier that comes with a HEPA filter. “Make sure it's a HEPA air purifier since these filter down to 0.3 microns and have a robust amount of studies done showing their efficacy.” HEPA filters remove at least 99.97 percent of airborne particles like dust, bacteria, and pollen, and are the gold standard for air purification.

It has been revealed that activated carbon filters are more porous and help get rid of gases and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that are commonly found in household items like surface cleaners and candles. These filters absorb molecules onto carbon and are best used in environments with strong odors or smoke.

With laundry machines, dishwashers, and fans all emitting their own noise, adding another loud appliance into the mix could be overkill, especially since air purifiers are meant to run the entire day.

Look for models that range from 10 to 30 decibels. A whisper is around 30 decibels, so expect air purifiers in this noise range to be almost virtually silent.

“Air purifiers need to be kept clean, and filters should be changed every six months,” Parikh says. Since air purifier filters are designed to collect and trap different-sized particles, contaminants, and hair, they get gunky pretty easily. This buildup could even reduce the efficiency and the air quality of the purifier if not cleaned often enough. Most air purifiers come with reusable filters, so just rinse them off in between replacements.

Recent findings suggest that app compatibility, savvy control panels, remotes, check filter indicators, and variable settings are beneficial features that make it easier to use your air purifier. If you want to monitor the air quality levels in your home or keep tabs on filter life, look for an air purifier that pairs with an app. If you’re easily overstimulated by loud noises, consider an air purifier that has different modes for adjusting the speed of the internal fan.

Sources indicate that air purifiers use a fan to draw air into the unit, then pass it through a series of filters to remove particles and contaminants. Said filters vary in effectiveness and normally target a specific concern like odors, smoke, and viruses. Once the air has passed through the fan and all of the appropriate filters, it is recirculated back into the room for a cleaner and healthier environment.

“Air purifiers filter out pollutants, improve air quality, remove infectious agents and pollen,” indicates Parikh. “They limit your level of exposure and reduce lung damage and flare-ups of underlying chronic conditions such as asthma attacks, COPD exacerbations, and heart issues.”.

“It can affect everyone’s health by causing inflammation and lung damage over time that may be either reversible or irreversible,” Parikh says. “It is especially dangerous for those with underlying heart disease, lung disease, pregnant women, children, and immunocompromised individuals.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that my favorite thing about San Juan? You can have a morning that feels plucked out of a history book, an afternoon that commits you entirely to the beach, and a night that’s topped off with a frosty Medalla, sweet rum cocktail, and flirty bachata dance. It’s glitzy yet lush, historic yet ever-evolving, a city delightfully full of contrasts, and one I will never run out of reasons to revisit.

Industry observers note that my father’s side of the family is from Puerto Rico, so I’ve been coming back to the island for years, and I love that there’s always another corner to get to know. There’s Old San Juan, with all its pastel-painted façades, galleries and shops, blue cobblestone streets, and tucked-away restaurants; Condado and Ocean Park for long, sea-salty afternoons by the ocean; and Santurce, where street murals, galleries, haute dining, and a lively bar scene bring a fresh, creative vibe to the city.

Of course, there’s no shortage of hotels in San Juan, but sometimes a vacation to the island’s capital calls for a little more room to sprawl, or a front door that opens onto a lush little neighborhood rather than a buzzy hotel lobby. The city’s best Airbnbs offer just that, along with wonderful amenities, whether it’s a private pool hidden behind swaying palms or a breezy courtyard for sipping on some local morning coffee.

Industry observers note that consider this your invitation to soak up the sun in Puerto Rico's capital for a few days. Read on for nine of the best Airbnbs in San Juan to consider for your next trip.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Conveniently, it's situated right in the heart of San Juan’s food and arts district and just a few steps from Ocean Park Beach.
